title: ‘Madden’: Why Christian Bale Ranks Raiders Owner Al Davis as One of His Favorite Characters and the Jewelry He Took Home From Set
description: Christian Bale says portraying Oakland Raiders owner Al Davis in “Madden” is one of his favorite roles from his four-decade career. That’s extremel
body:
Christian Bale says portraying Oakland Raiders owner Al Davis in “Madden” is one of his favorite roles from his four-decade career. That’s extremely high praise considering Bale’s resume is longer than a CVS receipt, and includes winning an Oscar (for “The Fighter”) and playing Batman three times. 

	So why did Bale enjoy playing the eccentric football team owner so much? 

	“He had so many just wonderful contradictions,” Bale told Variety at the Amazon MGM Studios film’s world premiere earlier this month. “He was such a strong character. He liked to intimidate people, you know; he said all this ‘Just win, baby’ and ‘Dominate.’ It’s a game of psychological intimidation and fear.”
	

	On the flip side, Davis had “one of the biggest hearts of anybody,” Bale said. “He took care of people. He kept this very quiet. He didn’t really like people knowing about how much he cared for others.”

	In truth, Davis, who owned the NFL team for 39 years, from 1972 until his death in 2011, lived the mantra of “Once a Raider, Always a Raider.” Bale explained: “He kept caring for [players] after they were long gone from the roster. But he was just an icon. He was a trailblazer, and he seemed to know what he wanted to do in life from a very, very early age and did it. It’s quite incredible and very, very unique.”



	

					Christian Bale as Al Davis and Nicolas Cage as John Madden in “Madden.”
									Amazon MGM Studios
	



	In “Madden,” now playing in theaters and streaming on Prime Video, director David O. Russell explores the special bond between Davis and the Raiders’ Super Bowl-winning coach John Madden (Nicolas Cage). The film follows their relationship as it evolves from owner and coach to a deeper, though sometimes complicated, friendship when Madden retires from coaching and starts a career in the broadcast booth.
	

	Since Bale and Cage are both famous for diving deep into their characters, O. Russell encouraged them to riff on set. One of their ad-libs made the trailer, with Bale’s Davis introducing Cage’s Madden to a hot new rap group — N.W.A. Another, riffing on the fact that Madden’s tour bus was loaned from Dolly Parton and the pair sing “9 to 5,” was left on the cutting room floor — though O. Russell wants to release it if the studio can clear the rights.

	“I’m used to working with David, and I love it,” Bale said. (“Madden” marks the actor and director’s fourth collaboration, following 2010’s “The Fighter,” 2013’s “American Hustle” and 2022’s “Amsterdam.”) “David writes beautiful scripts, so we obviously do that. But then he’s often shouting new lines out at us. He loves it when we start going off script as well, and so it creates a real atmosphere of fun and creativity, and it ends up looking incredible, having been imbued with life.” 



	

					Christian Bale and David O. Russell during the premiere’s after-party.
									Michael Buckner
	



	Aside from the focus on football, “Madden” also spotlights Al Davis’ love story with his wife Carol Davis, portrayed in the film by Sienna Miller. 

	“What was so moving was their absolute devotion to each other,” said Miller. “Al lived and breathed football. That was No. 1. The only thing that would keep him away from a game was his love for his wife.” 

	That devotion was epitomized when Carol suffered a stroke in 1979. “[Al] stayed by her bed. He slept in the hospital. He did not leave her side. I guess you’d hope that was the case, but the world stopped for him,” Miller said. “It was that love that I wanted to bring into the film.” [Carol Davis recovered and, after inheriting ownership of the team from Al, led the Raiders until her death in 2025.]

	As much passion as the Davises had for each other, they also had a passion for fashion. “Madden” includes a goofy montage where Al and Carol try on a myriad of snazzy ’80s getups, but the sequence doubles as a genuinely sweet tribute to their love. Did Bale take any of Davis’ jackets or his signature pinky ring home from set? 

	“I didn’t take any of the jackets, but I did take Super Bowl ring,” Bale admitted. “That’s in a very nice little box on a shelf.”
	

	After Davis, Bale is soon set to take on another legend — playing Lt. Vincent Hanna in Michael Mann’s long-awaited “Heat 2.”

	“I was very reticent because I thought, ‘Oh, these are legends. These are icons. Like, how can you compete with that?’” Bale said about taking on a role originated by Al Pacino. “Talking with Michael, well, he’s written an absolutely brilliant script. He’s a phenomenal director, and I thought, ‘All right, I’m a coward if I don’t try doing this.’ So, I’m enjoying figuring out how to play that one.”



	

					Christian Bale and his wife, Sibi Blazic, on the red carpet at the “Madden” world premiere.
									Earl Gibson III

schema.headline: ‘Madden’: Why Christian Bale Ranks Raiders Owner Al Davis as One of His Favorite Characters and the Jewelry He Took Home From Set

title: ‘Glee’ Reboot: ‘Sadness’ Over Naya Rivera and Cory Monteith’s Deaths Is ‘Going to Be a Part’ of the Show, Says Co-Creator Ian Brennan
description:
“Glee” co-creator Ian Brennan admits he wasn’t always open to the upcoming “Glee” reboot.

	“I wasn’t that excited about it,” he told me earlier th
body:
“Glee” co-creator Ian Brennan admits he wasn’t always open to the upcoming “Glee” reboot.

	“I wasn’t that excited about it,” he told me earlier this week at an FYC event for his latest television project “Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story.” “Every time it came up, it was like, ‘Why would you do that again?’ For whatever reason, in the last six months or so, I completely did a 180 about it. It just seems the idea is right. I think the time is right. Now I’m really excited about it. It’s going to be a lot of fun.”
	

	In September, creator Ryan Murphy revealed he had just completed the first script for a reboot. “Brad [Falchuk], Ian and I, who wrote all the first two seasons, have written something,” he told Entertainment Tonight. “I’ve been in touch with around 10 of the original cast members. It’s very sweet, and they all had a lot of questions, but they all were very enthusiastic about the idea.”

	Brennan told me, “You’re catching these characters at a totally different part of their life … The timing of these characters thinking, ‘Maybe that was the best time in my life, being in that choir in high school’ and then once you think that you’re like, ‘Oh, that show’s going to work.’”

	While a production start date has yet to be set, Brennan touched on how the reboot may handle the deaths of Finn actor Cory Monteith, who suffered a fatal accidental heroin overdose, and Naya Rivera, who played Santana and died after she drowned in 2020 while trying to save her four-year-old son during a boat outing.
	

	“We’re still figuring a lot of it out,” Brennan said. “That’s going to be part of it, that sadness and that loss. But still in all, I think [“Glee”] is too big of a thing to sort of let lay. There’s something about that feels right right now.”

	As for Brennan’s song picks for the reboot, he said, “We didn’t do enough Journey. We did almost all of Journey but there’s still a bunch of hits.”

	The “Monster” anthology is a far cry (or scream, for that matter) from “Glee.” I know [“Monster”] is a much different animal, but actually at its core like all writing it’s trying to get inside the head of someone else’s mind,” Brennan said. “I’m stunned at how fun it is to do this show.”

	Before Murphy suggested Lizzie Borden to his team they were working on three different seasons around Luigi Mangione, the 1984 New York City subway shooter Bernie Goetz and the Unabomber. “I don’t think it’s talking out of turn because we’re never going to do it,” Brennan said. “We were going to do like a triptych of Luigi Mangione, Bernie Goetz and Unabomber. It was really interesting about male rage, about vigilantes. And it was just hard to write. It was like pushing like a dead mule up a hill. Luigi, we don’t know anything about. Bernie Goetz is sort of interesting a bit in that sort of Michael Douglas in ‘Falling Down’ kind of way. Kaczynski is fascinating, very bright, a very strange mind, but nothing really sexy about that story really.”

	Ella Beatty stars in the show as the titular Lizzie Borden. She often returned home after a day of shooting covered in fake blood. “Shaving cream actually is a great hack to get fake blood off of your skin and out of your hair,” Beatty said, adding, “I feel like I was always covered in blood. I feel like I almost never wasn’t.”

	She joked that she “frequently” took “shaving cream baths.”

	Charlie Hunnam, who plays Lizzie’s father, said his love of axes began way before he signed on for the show. He actually has a collection of about a dozen axes. “Some of them are in my garage, some of them are in my pickup truck,” he said. “I have like a sick obsession. I cannot drive past a wood pile in L.A. or anywhere when a tree has been felled and they leave all of those rounds of wood on the road I have to like a complete crazy person pull over and fill my pickup truck with wood and then go cut it. I have a little back area in my office building, and I probably have three, four or five tons of chopped firewood.”

title: Caleb Hearon and Zooey Deschanel TIFF Dramedy ‘Trash Mountain’ Acquired by Magnolia Pictures
description: Magnolia Pictures has snatched up North American rights to “Trash Mountain,” a dramedy film starring Caleb Hearon, who co-wrote the script with Rub
body:
Magnolia Pictures has snatched up North American rights to “Trash Mountain,” a dramedy film starring Caleb Hearon, who co-wrote the script with Ruby Caster, and Zooey Deschanel. A theatrical release is in the works for next year. 

	“I Used to Go Here” filmmaker Kris Rey directs “Trash Mountain,” and Colin Trevorrow serves as producer. The movie held its premiere at the Toronto International Film Festival in September. 


	According to an official logline, “‘Trash Mountain’ follows the story of Gavin (Hearon), a young gay Chicago man who is forced to return to his hometown in rural Missouri following the death of his hoarder father. The story takes us on a journey of emotional acceptance and resilience as Gavin and his half-sister Abbi (Deschanel) navigate challenging family dynamics and their complicated relationships withthe past.” 
	

	Other cast members include Jacki Weaver, Jaboukie Young-White, Kyle Marvin and Holmes.

	“’Trash Mountain’ is such a funny, smart, joyful work, which is no surprise coming from the brilliant mind of Caleb Hearon,” said Magnolia Pictures co-CEOs Eamonn Bowles and Dori Begley. “We’re so excited to collaborate with Caleb, Kris, Colin and this fantastic cast to bring it to audiences.”

	Metronome Film Company presents, in association with Sight Unseen, Pigasus Pictures, Five Sticks Productions and Streeterville Productions. Rebecca Linfoot co-produced “Trash Mountain.” Executive producers include Zachary Spicer, Julia Lebedev, Eddie Vaisman, Hearon, Lilly Wachowski, Annys Hamilton, Carrie Holt De Lama, Kelley Sims, Chris Cafero, Scott L. Goldstein, George Rush and Willie Trieger.
	

	“’Trash Mountain’ is a film about home. The physical homes we reside in, the emotions that we make home in, the place where we grew up, and the way that many of us make home elsewhere when we’ve spilled out over the brims of our hometowns,” said Hearon. “I’ve been a fan of Magnolia films for a very long time and we’re honored to be partnering with them.”

	Hearon, a 31-year-old stand-up comedian and host of the “So True with Caleb Hearon” podcast, has seen his star rise in recent years, landing memorable supporting roles in films like “Pizza Movie,” “The Devil Wears Prada 2” and “Little Brother.” His other film credits include “Jurassic World: Dominion,” “I Used to Be Funny” and “Sweethearts.” Deschanel, best known for her turn as Jess in the long-running Fox sitcom “New Girl,” was last seen in the Prime Video holiday rom-com “Merv” with Charlie Cox. Her other recent big-screen credits include “Harold and the Purple Crayon” and “Trolls Band Together.”

	The deal was negotiated by Magnolia Pictures SVP of Acquisitions John Von Thaden and VP of Acquisitions Miranda Hill, and by CAA Media Finance and WME on behalf of the filmmakers.

	At Best Buy, shoppers can find everything from immersive sound systems for the cinephile to sleek coffee machines for the friend who has perfected their at-home latte routine. JBL’s latest soundbars and portable speakers make it easier to recreate the movie theater or concert experience at home, while Nespresso’s espresso machines are an appealing upgrade for anyone looking to upgrade their morning routine in the new year.
	

	Meanwhile, smart glasses are becoming an increasingly visible part of the fashion and entertainment conversation. Meta’s collaborations with Ray-Ban and Oakley have brought AI-powered wearables into the mainstream, combining recognizable eyewear silhouettes with hands-free cameras, audio and voice assistants. For a more practical gift, Brother’s wireless printers and label makers are particularly useful for creatives, aspiring screenwriters and anyone building a home office.

	Whether you’re shopping for a devoted film buff, a music obsessive, a fashion enthusiast or someone who simply loves a good gadget, these Best Buy finds make the perfect gift this holiday season:

The 7.1.4-channel soundbar features Dolby Atmos and DTS:X, a wireless subwoofer and detachable surround speakers that can be placed behind the sofa for more immersive sound. It’s particularly appealing for action movies, concerts and prestige TV marathons.	
		
	

		

						
			
	

	
					
		

										TOP RATED

		JBL’s Charge 6 is a versatile gift for the music lover who brings a playlist everywhere. The portable speaker delivers punchy bass, features AI Sound Boost to optimize audio and offers up to 28 hours of playtime with Playtime Boost enabled. Its waterproof, dustproof design makes it equally suited to beach days, backyard parties and weekend getaways.

It also comes in a range of colors.

The stainless-steel machine combines Nespresso’s single-serve brewing system with an integrated steam wand, allowing users to prepare everything from cappuccinos to flat whites with textured milk. It’s a particularly thoughtful gift for someone who spends a small fortune at their neighborhood café.	
		
	

		

						
			
	

	
					
		

					Ray-Ban Meta Wayfarer (Gen 2)		

	
		For the fashion-conscious tech enthusiast, Ray-Ban’s second-generation Meta Wayfarers combine one of the eyewear brand’s most recognizable silhouettes with hands-free technology. The smart glasses let wearers capture photos and videos, listen to music, make calls and interact with Meta AI using voice commands. They’re a particularly fun gift for travelers, content creators and anyone who wants to spend less time looking at a phone.	
		
	

		

						
			
	

	
					
		

					Oakley Meta Vanguard Sunglasses		

	
		Oakley’s Meta Vanguard glasses are designed for the athlete who loves tracking every adventure. The performance-focused smart glasses combine a built-in camera, open-ear audio and Meta AI with sporty wraparound frames and Oakley’s Prizm lenses. Designed with outdoor activities in mind, they’re an especially compelling gift for runners, cyclists and fitness enthusiasts looking to capture their workouts hands-free.

title: Marlon Jackson Reveals Stage Four Prostate Cancer Diagnosis: ‘Don’t Worry About It. God Got Me’
description:
Marlon Jackson, Michael Jackson‘s older brother who also sang in the Jackson 5, has revealed that he has stage four prostate cancer.

	He shared th
body:
Marlon Jackson, Michael Jackson‘s older brother who also sang in the Jackson 5, has revealed that he has stage four prostate cancer.

	He shared the health update while appearing as a guest on “The Farah Shammas Podcast.” When asked by Shammas how he stays healthy at age 69, he said, “I’ma break some news to you that you don’t know and tell people right now: God has me. He already he told me he has me. I’ve had cancer for four years.”
	

	When Shammas reacted with shock, he waved it away. “Oh, yes. But don’t worry about it. God got me. Everything is great.”

	Jackson said that he has had surgery to remove his prostate gland and has undergone radiation therapy. He insisted that he’s in good health and keeps active, saying, “Everything is fine. Everything is great. I walk almost four miles, four times a week. And that’s great for me.” He also shared that he hasn’t eaten beef or pork in almost 50 years and made additional changes to his diet after receiving the diagnosis. “I do away with sugar and I’m careful what I put in my body and try to take care of myself,” he said. “My doctor said, ‘You’re doing so much better than I thought.'”

	He had a sense of humor while addressing his prognosis, saying, “Bad grass don’t die, so I’m gonna be around for a long time.”

	Jackson is the sixth of Joe and Katherine Jackson’s ten children. Besides his twin, who died shortly after birth, Marlon was the closest in age to Michael Jackson, who was born one year after him. Marlon left the Jackson 5 in 1985, shortly after Michael, and released the solo album “Baby Tonight” in 1987. After that, he mostly left the music business and began to pursue real estate. He has made several public appearances recently while promoting the biopic “Michael.”

title: Judge Allows Trump to Sue New York Times Reporters Over Tax Fraud Claims
description: A judge has allowed President Trump to proceed with a $15 billion suit against the New York Times, finding a plausible claim that its reporters act
body:
A judge has allowed President Trump to proceed with a $15 billion suit against the New York Times, finding a plausible claim that its reporters acted recklessly in accusing Trump of tax fraud.

	Judge Steven Merryday denied the defendants’ motion to dismiss the lawsuit, holding that the book “Lucky Loser” includes a series of claims about Trump’s business dealings that are potentially defamatory.


	Though the book cites tax experts who stated that Trump’s conduct was “highly suspicious” and “smells like a crime,” the judge ruled that was not enough to state outright that Trump had committed tax fraud or tax evasion. Such a clear-cut judgment would require “an explicit opinion from a qualified source after a thorough examination of pertinent facts,” the judge ruled.
	

	Absent such a statement, the judge ruled that the reporters were venturing into risky territory.

	“They know that they don’t know, but they are undeterred,” he wrote.

	The book, published by Penguin Random House, included the allegation that Trump had obtained the equivalent of $400 million from his father, Fred, “much of it through fraudulent tax evasion schemes.” The book also asserted that Fred Trump had engaged in “likely tax fraud” when he gave his son gifts disguised as loans; and that the arrangement was designed to avoid gift and estate taxes.

	In his lawsuit, Trump argued that the statements were false because neither he nor his father had ever been charged with a tax crime.

	The New York Times published two articles drawn from the book in 2024. In the ruling, Merryday dismissed the claims pertaining to the first article, which focused on Trump’s relationship with TV producer Mark Burnett and the development of “The Apprentice.”
	

	The judge also tossed statements from the second article that focused on Trump’s school record. But the judge allowed Trump to sue over a statement from that article that authorities had investigated his “ties to the Mafia” and had found “violations of money laundering laws.”

	The same judge dismissed an earlier version of Trump’s lawsuit last year, finding it overlong and full of colorful but irrelevant detail. Trump’s lawyers refiled a more concise version a month later.

	The suit can now proceed to discovery and motions for summary judgment. The defendants in the case are the Times, three of its reporters, and Penguin Random House.

title: Netflix and Disney Alum Tendo Nagenda Joins Proximity Media as President
description: Veteran executive and producer Tendo Nagenda will join Proximity Media as president, company founders Ryan Coogler, Zinzi Coogler and Sev Ohanian a
body:
Veteran executive and producer Tendo Nagenda will join Proximity Media as president, company founders Ryan Coogler, Zinzi Coogler and Sev Ohanian announced on Thursday.

	“Tendo has spent his career working alongside talented filmmakers, championing original ideas and helping make projects that resonate with audiences around the world,” the Cooglers and Ohanian, who most recently produced the Oscar-winning film “Sinners,” said in a joint statement.
	

	“As Proximity continues to grow across film, television and nonfiction, we’re excited to have his creative instincts and experience helping guide this next chapter,” the trio continued. “He shares our belief in the power of storytelling to connect people, challenge perspectives and create meaningful impact, and we’re thrilled to welcome him to the team.”

	As president, Nagenda will oversee all aspects of creative development and production across Proximity’s film, television and nonfiction divisions, reporting directly to the founders. In addition to guiding the multimedia company’s slate of projects — including the highly anticipated “X-Files” series at Hulu, starring Danielle Deadwyler and Himesh Patel, and Marvel’s “Black Panther 3” — Nagenda will also help shape the company’s broader business strategy.

	Nagenda will work alongside Terra Potts, who oversees marketing, operations and the “In Proximity” podcast, and Proximity co-founder Ludwig Göransson, who oversees music. The heads of film, TV and nonfiction will report directly to Nagenda. He will assume the role on Nov. 30.

	“I’m honored and excited to join Ryan, Zinzi, Sev and the entire Proximity team,” said Nagenda. “Their commitment to ambitious, meaningful storytelling reflects everything I’ve always believed in, and I look forward to building on what they’ve created, collaborating with extraordinary filmmakers and creators, and bringing compelling new stories to audiences around the world.”
	

	Nagenda’s extensive entertainment resume includes key positions at Netflix and Walt Disney Studios. At Netflix, he served as VP of original film, where he helped build the streamer’s original film slate and oversaw a range of acclaimed projects, including Spike Lee’s “Da 5 Bloods,” “The Old Guard,” “Ma Rainey’s Black Bottom,” “The Harder They Fall” and “Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery.” Before Netflix, he served as executive VP of production at Walt Disney Studios, overseeing live-action films including “Beauty and the Beast,” “Cinderella,” “Saving Mr. Banks,” “Mulan,” “A Wrinkle in Time” and “Queen of Katwe.”

	In 2022, Nagenda founded 10 by Ten Entertainment, a production company focused on developing and producing original stories from “distinctive and underrepresented perspectives.” His first produced feature was 2024’s “The Book of Clarence,” written and directed by Jeymes Samuel and released theatrically by Sony.

	Nagenda’s appointment comes as Proximity Media continues to expand its slate across film, television and nonfiction. In June, the company entered into a multiyear television deal with Netflix to develop an exclusive slate of scripted and unscripted projects. Proximity Media’s television division is behind series including Marvel’s “Ironheart” and the animated “Black Panther” spinoff “Eyes of Wakanda”; the National Geographic docuseries “Hurricane Katrina: A Race Against Time”; “Stephen Curry: Underrated”; “Homeroom”; and “Anthem.”

title: ‘The Year of the Ghost,’ About Misogyny in China, Wins Best Film at IDFA Documentary Festival
description: Louis HotHotHot‘s “The Year of the Ghost” won best film in the International Competition section of leading documentary festival IDFA on Thursday.
body:
Louis HotHotHot‘s “The Year of the Ghost” won best film in the International Competition section of leading documentary festival IDFA on Thursday.

	The award is accompanied by a €15,000 ($16,462) cash prize.

	The film, a co-production between Netherlands and China, focuses on the director’s mother and sister in China following his father’s death. He explores how misogyny has affected the lives of the women in his family across the generations.
	

	The film was told with “bold honesty, a rare attention to detail, cinematic curiosity and love,” the jury said. They added that they were “astonished by this work of singular artistic vision exploring deep family dynamics and connections, set against the wider societal forces and gender constraints inherited across generations.”

	The award for best directing, and a €5,000 prize, in the International Competition went to Joël Richmond Mathieu Akafou for “Lonan Tché,” a co-production between France, Italy, Ivory Coast and Senegal.

	The film is an intimate double portrait of two young men from Ivory Coast who fled to Europe together. Kader now has legal residency in Italy, while Inza is undocumented in France. For both, the gap between expectation and reality proves almost impossible to bridge.

	The jury commented, “Through its deeply attaching characters and the subtitle proximity the filmmaker established with them, the film depicts two overgrown kids in their quest for a dream they might never reach, elevating them to almost mythical figures, enduring their human condition.”

	The award for best editing in the International Competition went to “The Year of the Ghost,” with editing by HotHotHot and Chris van Oers.
	

	The award for best cinematography in the International Competition went to “Bardi” (Morocco) by Tala Hadid, with cinematography by Hadid.

	The special mention for International Competition went to “Hazara Town” by Khadim Dai (Belgium, Australia, Germany).

	The jury members of the International Competition were Barbara Orlicz-Szczypuła, Hania Mroué, Katy Léna N’diaye, Laura Poitras and Luuk Bouwman.

	The award for best film in the Envision Competition went to Riccardo Giacconi for “Memories of Lightning” (France, Italy). The award is accompanied by a €15,000 cash prize.

	The jury said it was a “film that captures the silence of things falling, like distant flashes of lightning that are sure to herald the storm.”

	The award for best directing (worth €5,000) in the Envision Competition went to Yuula Benivolski for “The Black Box Is Orange” (Canada). The award for outstanding artistic contribution went to Sibilla Scinti Roger for her work on “Memories of Lightning” (France, Italy).

	The special mention for Envision Competition went to “Memories” (Belgium, France) by Anna Falguères.

	The jury members of the Envision Competition were Firouzeh Khosrovani, Hélder Beja, Hicham Khalidi, Isabel Pagliai and Jonathan Perel.

	The DocLab Award for immersive non-fiction went to Michał Stankiewicz for “Being in You” (Poland). The award is accompanied by a €5,000 cash prize.

	The jury said, “Through a tender exploration of life and death, this project invited us to see how VR can be a tool to memorialize while also bringing a sense of embodied presence.”

	The special mention for the DocLab Competition for immersive non-fiction went to “Shifting Connections” (Taiwan) by Tungyen Chou.

	The jury members of the DocLab Competition for immersive non-fiction were Blake Kammerdiener, Natalie Paneng and Roel Wouters.

	Ant Hampton won the DocLab Award for digital storytelling with “All the Downtime” (Netherlands, Belgium). The award is accompanied by a €5,000 cash prize.

	“The work invites us to see the increasing entanglements between technocapitalism, precarious labor conditions, automation of human work, disregards of natural ecosystems and the new warlords of corporate fascism,” said the jury.
	

	The special mention for the DocLab Competition for digital storytelling went to “Plum Road Tea Dream” (Belgium) by Samuel Baidoo.

	The jury members of the DocLab Competition for digital storytelling were Abel Enklaar, Claudix Vanesix and Pegah Tabassinejad.

	The award for best first feature across all sections went to “Hazara Town” by Khadim Dai (Belgium, Australia, Germany). The award is accompanied by a €5,000 prize.

	The special mention went to “She Was Not Alone” (Iraq, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, U.S.) by Hussein Al-asadi.

	The jury members were Gianluca Matarrese, Gugi Gumilang and Ketevan Kipiani.

title: ‘GTA 6’ Upsets Conservatives: Fox News Tells Fans to ‘Grow Up’ as Clavicular and More Manosphere Influencers Complain About Lucia
description: “Grand Theft Auto VI” is poised to break sales records and could even impact the larger economy as scores of fans take the day off work to cause di
body:
“Grand Theft Auto VI” is poised to break sales records and could even impact the larger economy as scores of fans take the day off work to cause digital mayhem. But some right-wing pundits aren’t thrilled with all of the attention the video game is getting.

	Fox News had a roundtable discussion on the Nov. 19 episode of “Outnumbered” about the game and adults who take the day off to play it, and clips of the discussion posted on X by journalist Acyn Torabi have gained attention.
	

	“Outnumbered” co-host Harris Faulkner criticized fans taking paid time off as shirking their civic duties, saying, “If this generation wants to preach about affordability, but they’re willing to cost billions of dollars in revenue loss on a day like today to go play a game, that probably tells you everything you need to know … Get yourself to work.”

	Fox News contributor Paul Mauro agreed, saying, “You’re taking off of work, you’re abdicating your responsibilities to whoever it is in your life so you can do this nonsense? I mean, c’mon, grow up.”

	Mauro was also upset with the game’s violence and how he thinks it could impact children, saying, “This is almost the equivalent of giving [a kid] a gun at an age when they don’t understand the responsibility.”

	Meanwhile, Manosphere influencers are frustrated that the game encourages players to treat main character Jason’s girlfriend, Lucia, with respect.

	Clavicular took to X on Nov. 18 to write, “‘GTA 6’ is insanely cucked, half of the missions are jestermaxing and simping for girls.”
	

	Myron Gaines wrote on X on Nov. 19, “Despite the game getting solid first-day reviews, this is yet another example of how political correctness, inclusivity and feminism has destroyed a legendary game series … The main character gets cucked by his gf the whole time …”

	Zack Hoyt, better known online as Asmongold, complained during a stream of the game that “I had to watch a stupid TV show with her, rub her feet and listen to her friends’ stories about Snapchat … Do I have go to the corner store and buy her some tampons too?”

	Despite chatter from commentators, “GTA 6” is breaking internet usage records and is already one of the best-reviewed games of all time.

title: California Couple Found Dead: Suit Claims Water Heater May Have Gone Years Without Inspection
description:
California Couple Found Dead
                          Homeowners May Have Ignored Water Heater W
body:
California Couple Found Dead
                          Homeowners May Have Ignored Water Heater Warnings
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              November 19, 2026
                            1:00 PM PST
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
              The California couple who died from carbon monoxide poisoning after a birthday party may have been sleeping near a dangerous water heater that hadn't been professionally inspected in years ... this according to a new lawsuit.
      
    
              According to court docs, obtained by TMZ, the kids of Jay and Kristen Ruskey claim homeowners Ben and Robin Korman either failed to have the home's water heater and exhaust system inspected or serviced by a qualified technician in the years leading up to their parents' deaths ... or had been warned about problems with the venting system and failed to fix them.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
              The allegations raise new questions about whether the deadly incident could have been prevented ... particularly because the lawsuit claims the Kormans knew or should have known about dangerous conditions inside their California home.
      

              The lawsuit also alleges the only carbon monoxide detector in or immediately outside the couple's guest bedroom had been disconnected from its electrical wiring before they arrived ... leaving them without a functioning detector to alert them to dangerous gas levels.
      
    
              As we reported ... Jay and Kristen attended a birthday celebration at the home on February 7 before spending the night. Early the next morning, Kristen called 911 after Jay began experiencing severe medical distress, including vomiting and seizure-like symptoms.
      
    
              They told authorities John had ingested a mushroom-based psychedelic edible, declined a suggestion to visit the ER, and went back to sleep. They were discovered unresponsive hours later and pronounced dead at the property.
      
    
              The couple's kids are suing the Kormans and the water heater manufacturer, alleging negligence and product defects contributed to their parents' deaths.

title: Cincinnati Zoo Hippo Fiona Dies After Swallowing Child's Hat
description:
Fiona the Hippo
                          Dead at 9 ...
                          Swallowed Kid's
body:
Fiona the Hippo
                          Dead at 9 ...
                          Swallowed Kid's Hat
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              November 19, 2026
                            1:20 PM PST
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  November 19, 2026
                                2:23 PM PST
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
              Fiona -- a popular hippo at the Cincinnati Zoo and Botanical Gardens -- has died after swallowing a child's hat ... the zoo announced on Thursday.
      
    
              The zoo posted photos paying tribute to Fiona on Facebook ... writing that she didn't make it despite the veterinary and keeper teams' best efforts.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
              The Cincinnati Zoo stated Fiona ate a hat last week. The vets tried to remove the hat from Fiona's system, but they ultimately couldn't.
      

              The zoo is asking the community to keep Fiona's keepers and others who tried to help her in their prayers.
      
    
      
      Fiona’s care team tried a new approach today to help her pass the hat she swallowed. With a vibration plate borrowed from a local horse farm, the team encouraged Fiona to stand on the platform throughout the day. Her team continues to provide care for her around the clock. https://t.co/HJDhGx15kq
              @CincinnatiZoo
          
  
    
              According to the local outlet WLWT 5, Fiona swallowed a knit hat that ended up in her enclosure after a child threw it into the air. It hit a fan and somehow slipped through a tiny gap into Fiona's habitat.
      
    
              The zoo stated, "We probably couldn't make that happen again if we tried. It was clearly an accident."
      
    
              Fiona was born prematurely in January 2017 ... weighing just 29 pounds -- which is 25 pounds less than the previous lowest recorded weight for a member of her species.
      
    
              Her recovery gained a national following ... and resulted in T-shirts and children's books being made.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
              Remember ... the Cincinnati Zoo and Botanical Gardens is the same zoo where Harambe -- a beloved gorilla -- was shot to death back in 2016 after a child fell into his enclosure.
      
    
              Fiona -- who had a younger brother named Fritz -- was just 9 years old when she died.

              Bruno Mars is grieving the loss of his dad, Peter Hernandez.
      
    
              The singer announced Peter's passing on social media Thursday by sharing a series of personal photos and memories.

              He was 74.

description:
'Can't Hardly Wait' Cast
                          We Can't Hardly Wait to Do It Again!!!
body:
'Can't Hardly Wait' Cast
                          We Can't Hardly Wait to Do It Again!!!
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              November 19, 2026
                            2:00 PM PST
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
              The "Can't Hardly Wait" cast can't hardly wait for a sequel ... because a few of them are really pushing for their own little high school reunion, TMZ has learned.
      
    
              Peter Facinelli -- who starred in the 1998 teen rom-com -- tells TMZ ... the film's fandom is still going strong, saying ... "I brought Mike Dexter back for Halloween, and weeks later the internet is still talking about it."
      
    
        Waiting for your permission to load the Instagram Media.
      
    
              He tells us ... "A 'Can't Hardly Wait' sequel is the one high school reunion everyone actually wants to go to. Would be so fun to get the whole gang back together and see where they ended up."
      

              Peter even gave us the elevator pitch, saying ... "If we're lucky, LoveBurger might finally play a song -- and maybe, just maybe, if I play my cards right I can finally get Amanda Beckett back."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
              Fellow cast member Joel Michaely tells TMZ ... they're not the only ones who want a sequel, saying ... "People have been clamoring for us to do a reunion movie for years. Now is the time for our 30th anniversary in 2028. While we all still look hot."
      
    
              Joel is encouraging fans to make their voices heard to sway the studios, adding ... "We need Sony to make it or partner with a streaming service like Netflix or Amazon, so tell them you want to see it."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
              Producer Johnny Ryan Jr. tells TMZ ... he and Kenan Thompson have been trying to produce a reunion film for years, and have even talked to the cast about it.
      
    
              He says Sony's dragging their feet, explaining ... "Sony told us they weren't sure if fans would want to see a reunion but the fans have spoken and they want it as much as we do."
      
    
              You heard 'em, Sony! What're you hardly waitin' for?!?

Ronnie's always dreamed of owning a house by the beach, but he's not ditching the Hollywood Hills just yet ... we're told he's keeping his home there as his main residence.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
              And when Ronnie wants a little oceanfront R&R, he'll have plenty of room to spread out ... the 6,700-square-foot mansion boasts four bedroom suites, five bathrooms, a massive kitchen with marble countertops and walls of glass overlooking the coastline.
      
    
              The luxurious digs also feature a private gym, bar lounge, a potential home theater and an infinity pool that practically spills into the Pacific.
